source.title: Higher Dimensional Spiral Delone Sets
source.quote: It is not clear to the authors whether a spiral Delone set with asymptotic density r = V_n^{-1} can exists in any dimension n >= 3.
source.quote_note: Words retain the original 'can exists'; the typeset formula is transcribed in ASCII. Quote is below 40 words.

definition_checked.radii: s_k=k^(1/n)u_k for k>=1, u_k in S^(n-1)
definition_checked.Delone: Uniform positive all-pair separation and uniformly bounded distance from every ambient point to the set.
definition_checked.density: For every bounded measurable X with Lebesgue-null boundary, # {k:s_k in R X}/R^n tends to r*lambda_n(X).
definition_checked.normalization: r=1/V_n, where V_n is n-dimensional unit-ball volume.
definition_checked.equidistribution: Spherical-cap frequencies for the entire direction sequence tend to normalized surface measure.
definition_checked.not_required: The paper does not require a continuous spiral, bounded distance between consecutive indices, primitive lattice directions, pairwise distinct directions, or a transitive-map orbit.

normalization_checks: Rendered page 22 visually shows V_n with superscript -1, not the volume V_(n-1).
Rendered page 23 repeats the superscript inverse in the explicit question.
Taking X=unit ball forces floor(R^n)/R^n ->1 = r V_n.
